description: We are a bunch of enthusiastic individuals aiming to learn from this experience.
summary: Fallow Clock is a tool made for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It helps farmers understand when there soil is bare and at risk of erosion due to heavy rainfall. Using 25 years of NASA weather data and satellite images, it turns a full field year into a 365-day ring showing soil cover and rainfall risk. Our biggest discovery was that fields are actually protected by leftover crop residue during winter, while the real risk comes in spring (March 24 to June 14), when 34% of the yearly erosive rain falls. Farmers can test different planting dates and cover crops. In Story County, cereal rye reduced bare days from 104 to 62, while Monona County already had only 7 bare days, showing that not every field needs extra intervention.
details:
Fallow Clock is a fun app that provides a full-field year in 365 days width ring showing cover and rainfall risk each year. Farmers can explore corn and soybean rotations, experiment with planting dates, replay extreme rainfall events, and test out potential futures for their fields.

The most important thing we discovered was the difference, and it was not what we thought. NASA data from a 25-year window revealed that crop residue lies above a blanket of winter soil, as would be expected in the Midwest, instead of bare fields over winter. But the real danger is in the spring, when the field is bare from March 24 to June 14, receiving 34% of the year's erosive precipitation.

Here's an example: We also observed the first autumn killing frost showing up 6.8 days later per decade, leaving more window of time for cover crops between harvest and first frost.

In Story County, for example, the tool has recommended cereal rye as a way to cut bare days from 42 and modeled erosion exposure by 27 percent at a cost of $62/hectare.But in Monona County, the crop is already pretty well protected, so the tool doesn't recommend wasting our dollars.

We integrate Landsat, Sentinel-2 and USDA data, as well as NASA POWER, with Python, React and three.js. Unlike others, Fallow Clock displays uncertainty, separates observed data from modeled predictions, and only recommends action at a field when it is genuinely needed.
